answer: The passage is the bullet point under 'Naming Conventions' in the CRMbase introduction. The original (v7.3-current) wording read: "Properties that have identical domain and range are either symmetric or transitive. Instantiating a symmetric property implies that the same relation holds for both the domain-to-range and the range-to-domain directions. An example of this is E53 Place. P122 borders with: E53 Place. The names of symmetric properties have no parenthetical form, because reading in the range-to-domain direction is the same as the domain-to-range reading. Transitive asymmetric properties, such as E4 Period. P9 consists of (forms part of): E4 Period, have a parenthetical form that relates to the meaning of the inverse direction." Wolfgang Schmidle flagged it (thread t1797, Oct 2024) as needing reformulation. Christian-Emil Smith Ore pointed out the actual flaw: having identical domain and range is NOT a sufficient condition for a property to be symmetric or transitive (counter-example: P152 has parent (is parent of) has identical domain/range but is neither symmetric nor transitive), and the opening sentence 'Properties that have identical domain and range are either symmetric or transitive' is simply false as stated (an even 'fixed' version, 'either symmetric, asymmetric, or neither', was noted as a tautology). Martin Doerr argued the whole paragraph was redundant patching, since symmetry/transitivity/reflexivity are already properly defined in the Terminology section, and repeating them under Naming Conventions only creates a maintenance pitfall (as just happened). He proposed shortening it to just the point actually relevant to naming conventions: the fact that symmetric properties have no parenthetical form. This was formalized as issue 686 and put to an E-VOTE in March 2025 (thread t1817), which passed unanimously (Wolfgang Schmidle, Martin Doerr, Christian-Emil implicitly, Oyvind Eide, Pat Riva, Athanasios Velios all voted YES). The final replacement text (adopted for CIDOC CRM v7.3+) is: "The names of symmetric properties have no parenthetical form, because reading in the range-to-domain direction is the same as the domain-to-range reading. An example of this is E53 Place. P122 borders with: E53 Place. See the definition of 'symmetric' in the section 'Terminology'." The reference to transitive/asymmetric properties (e.g. E4 Period. P9 consists of (forms part of): E4 Period) was dropped entirely as redundant with the Terminology section.
queries_run: search "properties whose domain and range are the same class symmetric transitive" -k 10
